title: An Arm Made of Smart Servos: A Position Command That Is Quantised, Slow to Arrive and Answered by a Spring, and How to Hold a Pose Anyway

questions.question: What does a computer send to a smart serial servo?
options: A torque, which the servo's motor applies
A voltage for the motor
A position goal, to a small controller of the servo's own
A speed, integrated by the servo
questions.explanation: The servo has its own position loop. The computer sends where to go and reads back where it is.

questions.question: A step of 4096 to a turn is:
options: 0.00153 rad, which is 1.07 mm at 0.7 m
0.088 rad, which is 61 mm at 0.7 m
0.00153 degrees
0.0153 rad, which is 10.7 mm at 0.7 m
questions.explanation: A turn of 6.283 rad over 4096 steps. At 0.7 m from the shaft one step is 1.07 mm at the tool, from one joint.

questions.question: The bus took how long for six servos at 1 Mbit/s and at 115 200 bit/s?
options: 14.3 ms and 2.98 ms
2.98 ms and 14.3 ms
2.98 ms at both: the servos set it
0.298 ms and 1.43 ms
questions.explanation: One packet out and six replies back, at ten bit times a byte. That is 336 Hz at best on the fast wire and 70 Hz on the slow one.

questions.question: A load of 2 N m drooped the joint by:
options: 0.00153 rad, one step
Nothing: the servo holds its goal
0.133 rad: load over stiffness
questions.explanation: A shifted goal left it 0.0002 rad off. The servo's loop is a spring of 15 N m/rad, and 2 over 15 is 0.133 rad. Shifting the goal by the load over the stiffness left 0.0002 rad.

questions.question: Why is the lag larger at 20 Hz than at 100 Hz?
options: The servo's speed limit is lower at 20 Hz
The bus sends fewer bits at 20 Hz
The goals arrive as a staircase and the spring follows it late
The rounding is coarser at 20 Hz
questions.explanation: 97 ms against 77 ms. Between goals the servo is chasing the last one. Faster updates shrink that part of the lag, down to the servo's own 73 ms.

questions.question: What limits how fast a large step is covered?
options: The bus rate
The resolution of the encoder
The stiffness of the servo's loop
The servo's speed limit: 0.39 s for 1 rad at 3 rad/s
questions.explanation: The servo turns no faster than 3 rad/s, so a radian takes at least a third of a second however quickly the goal arrived.
